newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen rising, 125.40 in sight.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen rising, 125.40 in sight.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is expected to edge upwards on Monday, retaining its firmness from last week, traders said.

"Straight bond launches have been relatively sparse, which means there is still a lot of money (being held by investors), and the dollar has been weak against the yen since U.S. interest rates were kept steady at (last week's) Federal Open Market Committee meeting. These factors have supported JGBs," said a trader for a trust bank's securities unit.
The market's primary focus is now on Tokyo share prices, a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
"There are no fresh trading incentives right now, other than (moves in) Tokyo share prices. If share prices continue to fall, JGBs will test the upside," the trader said.
Technical charts have turned positive, another factor which would support JGBs, the second trader said.
However traders said they felt JGBs were unlikely to have an easy time posting further gains, and that the current uptrend was not expected to continue much longer.
"The recent uptrend has been too fast, and a further rise will not be that easy. JGBs will likely have a hard time rising above 125.41, a key chart point," the second trader said.
The first trader said the recent bullishness of JGBs was reminiscent of early April, when they posted record highs.

"When JGBs rose in early April, they hit their peak on the day of the auction for super-long 20-year JGBs, and we are in a similar situation now. So I think JGBs will remain firm at the beginning of the week, but I'm not so sure that they will remain strong by the end of the week," he said.

Traders said the Finance Ministry was likely to hold an auction for 20-year JGBs on Tuesday. The bonds would likely have a coupon rate of 3.0 or 3.1 percent, judging from current market conditions, they said.
